tweetText: Top intelligence agencies warn that AI cyber threats will soon affect individuals and businesses. This is a wake-up call to strengthen cybersecurity measures now. via AI News.

Sakana AI launched Fugu, a multi-agent model to reduce risks from relying on a single AI vendor. This matters as it helps enterprises avoid operational vulnerabilities and enhances flexibility in AI deployments. via AI News

L’Oréal is integrating Maybelline's virtual makeup try-on feature into ChatGPT, announced at VivaTech 2026. This partnership enhances shopping experiences and showcases AI's role in beauty and consumer interaction. via AI News.
Omio is using OpenAI to create smarter travel conversations and speed up product development. This shift to an AI-native approach could revolutionize how we plan our trips. via OpenAI News

OpenAI launched Daybreak tools like Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber to help organizations identify and fix vulnerabilities efficiently. This could significantly enhance cybersecurity for businesses worldwide. via OpenAI News

OpenAI has launched Patch the Planet, an initiative to assist open-source maintainers in identifying and fixing vulnerabilities using AI and expert support. This effort is crucial for strengthening the security and reliability of open-source software. via OpenAI News
Major tech companies are laying off employees in 2026, citing AI as a key reason. This trend highlights the growing impact of AI on job markets and workforce changes. via TechCrunch AI

OpenAI has launched a new initiative aimed at identifying and fixing bugs in open source software. This effort is important for enhancing security and stability in the open source community. via TechCrunch AI

The AI industry is embracing a new concept called "the loop," allowing multiple AI agents to operate endlessly in the background. This innovation could significantly enhance efficiency and automation across various applications. via TechCrunch AI

AI chipmaker Groq has raised $650M and is refocusing on its neocloud business while hiring new executives after Nvidia's $20B not-acqui-hire deal. This move signals their ambition to strengthen their position in the competitive AI market. via TechCrunch AI
